title: Review the book-tax reconciliation — Halvorsen Inc.
instructions: Halvorsen Inc., a calendar-year C corporation, has pretax book income of $850,000 for 2025. A staff preparer drafted Schedule M-1 from the adjusted trial balance. Review it, then resolve the diagnostics. Tick every amount that is wrong and enter the correct amount.

exhibits.title: Selected trial balance data (2025)
exhibits.content:
| Account | Book amount |
|---|---:|
| Pretax book income | 850,000 |
| Federal income tax expense | 178,500 |
| Business meals (50% deductible) | 24,000 |
| Client entertainment (golf outings) | 9,000 |
| Fines and penalties (EPA violation) | 5,000 |
| Premiums on officer life insurance (Halvorsen is beneficiary) | 6,000 |
| Municipal bond interest income | 14,000 |
| Dividend income from a 25%-owned domestic corporation | 40,000 |
| Book depreciation | 120,000 |
| Bad debt expense (allowance method) | 18,000 |

Tax depreciation (Form 4562): **$185,000**. Accounts actually written off in 2025: **$11,000**. Total assets at year-end: **$6.2 million**.

parts.prompt: Review the prepared Schedule M-1 and taxable income.

rows.label: Expenses recorded on books not deducted on the return
rows.explanation: Meals 50% (12,000) + entertainment (9,000) + fines (5,000) + officer life insurance (6,000) + excess of bad debt expense over write-offs (7,000) = **39,000**. The preparer missed the fine (§162(f)).

rows.label: Income recorded on books not included on the return
Deductions on the return not charged against book income
rows.explanation: Only the **excess** of tax over book depreciation: 185,000 − 120,000 = **65,000**.

rows.label: Dividends-received deduction included on Schedule M-1
rows.explanation: The DRD is a **special deduction** taken on Form 1120 line 29b after the M-1 total, so it does not belong on M-1: **0**.

parts.prompt: Choose the correct resolution for each diagnostic.

rows.label: Book depreciation (120,000) differs from Form 4562 depreciation (185,000).
options: Expected — report the 65,000 excess on Schedule M-1
Use book depreciation on the return
rows.answer: Expected — report the 65,000 excess on Schedule M-1
rows.explanation: Tax depreciation methods differ from book; only the difference reconciles.

rows.label: The trial balance has a balance in "Fines and penalties" but Schedule M-1 has no matching add-back.
options: Add back the fine on Schedule M-1
Treat it as a capital expenditure
rows.answer: Add back the fine on Schedule M-1
rows.explanation: Fines paid to a government for violating a law are not deductible (§162(f)).

rows.label: The dividend deduction appears on both Schedule M-1 and line 29b.
options: Remove it from Schedule M-1; claim it on line 29b only
rows.answer: Remove it from Schedule M-1; claim it on line 29b only

rows.label: Total assets at year-end: $6.2 million. Confirm the reconciliation schedule.
rows.explanation: Schedule M-3 is required when total assets are $10 million or more.
